- When sentiment is positive (≥0.5), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 10–15% above recent peak.
- In absence of sentiment, model exhibits persistent mean reversion bias; adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% per day if price is above 72.00.
- If 3–5 consecutive days of low sentiment (0.00), model underestimates; add 0.5–1.0% to forecast to counteract downward bias.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently underestimates in early window (days 1–7); apply 0.8–1.2% upward bias to first 7 days.
- If sentiment is negative (≤-0.5), model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid missing downside risk.
- Model shows lag in reacting to sentiment shifts; delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days if sentiment changes abruptly.
